subject: Re: Production latency spike — request for credit and trial extension
messages:
From: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@brooklinehealth.com>
To: support@redwood.ai; sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 5 Oct 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency spike — impact on nightly ETL and request for credits

Hi team,

We saw a recurring latency regression in your hosted inference endpoint (model: rdx-llama-34b-instruct) between 02:10–04:40 UTC on 2025-10-05. The increased tail latency caused our nightly ETL workers to time out on ~18% of requests and delayed several downstream jobs that are timing-sensitive for morning charting.

Our SREs traced it to sustained 95th percentile token latency jumping from ~180ms to ~1200ms across multiple regions. We opened INC-20251005-42 with your on-call but would like clarity on root cause and an offer of goodwill credits or a trial extension while we evaluate a migration to Dedicated.

We are evaluating renewal options in Q4 and this incident materially impacts our decision. Can you confirm:
- the scope and root cause (if known)
- any immediate mitigations (rate-limiting, autoscale) you applied
- a concrete credit or trial extension you can provide to offset the impact and help with our evaluation

Thanks,
Alex Monroe
Head of AI Platforms | Brookline Health
alex.monroe@brooklinehealth.com
+1 (415) 555-0142
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@brooklinehealth.com>
Cc: support@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 5 Oct 2025 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — impact on nightly ETL and request for credits

Hi Alex — first, I’m really sorry for the disruption. We saw the same anomaly in our telemetry and our SRE team cut a high-priority incident (INC-20251005-42).

Quick answers while we continue the investigation:
- Scope/root cause: preliminary analysis points to a kernel scheduling regression in the autoscaling hosts that caused intermittent GC-like stalls in the inference runtime. We have a mitigation in place (rolling restart and kernel patch) that reduced the incidents after 03:15 UTC; we’re still validating the full timeline. Full postmortem and RCA to follow.
- Immediate mitigations: we applied a temporary routing policy to direct requests for your account to stable capacity pools and bumped replica count for your endpoints for the next 24 hours.
- Credit/trial: we want to make this right. I can offer a $2,000 service credit applied to your account plus a 45-day complimentary extension of your trial/paid term to give you breathing room for the evaluation. If you prefer a custom amount tied to observed failed/late requests, we can compute a usage-aligned credit and share the math.

I understand the renewal timing is sensitive; if you’re available, I’d like to schedule a 30-minute call with me, our SRE lead, and your engineering lead to walk through the timeline and the remediation plan. Are you available Mon 10/6 09:00–11:00 PT?

Apologies again — we’ll stay on this until you’re comfortable.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Production latency spike — impact on nightly ETL and request for credits

Alex — thanks for your patience. Quick update and what we’re doing: 

1) What happened: our initial RCA shows a kernel scheduling regression on a subset of autoscale hosts that produced repeated runtime stalls during peak tokenization for your workload (INC-20251005-42). Full postmortem is in progress; we will share the report by EOD 10/07.

2) Mitigation timeline: rolling patch and routing adjustments were applied and verified; the 95th percentile latency returned to baseline by ~03:35 UTC on 10/05. We attached a small timeline screenshot showing the spike window.

3) Compensation: per internal approval, we’ve applied a $2,000 service credit to Brookline Health (credit memo attached: credit-memo-78912.pdf). We also added a 45-day complimentary extension to your account to cover evaluation time. Billing will confirm the credit entry within 1–2 business days.

4) Next steps:
- I’ll schedule a 30-minute call with our SRE lead and your engineering lead to walk the timeline — is Tue 10/7 09:00 PT good for you?
- CS will reach out to coordinate renewal conversations and ensure you have a migration plan to Dedicated if you want more predictable capacity.

Attachments: incident-timeline-snapshot.png (screenshot of 95th percentile token latency), credit-memo-78912.pdf (billing memo)

Again, sorry for the disruption. If you’d like a different credit calculation tied to measured failed/late requests, tell me and I’ll run the numbers.

Best regards,
